text:
Nora K.: Heads up  candidate (Mateo V) emailed with a few specific logistic requests for Wednesday's onsite. He uses a mobility wheelchair and needs an elevator-only route from the garage to the 5th floor lab. Also asked whether we can provide a left-handed ergonomic keyboard + vertical mouse.
Dev (Recruiter): Noted. He also asked if the coding portion can run on Windows/VS2022 since his repo uses .NET. Any objections?
Aisha (People Ops): Windows + VS2022 fine. We'll provision a loaner Windows machine with VS2022 + .NET SDK and the test harness. Mateo prefers Visual Studio with dark theme, but that's just a preference.
Facilities Bot: Elevator-only route confirmed from East Garage elevator -> Lobby -> Service Elevator -> 5th floor lab. Signage to be placed at East Garage entrance. Accessibility escort available on arrival.
accessibility-bot: Wheelchair access checklist: reserve wide-access room (door >= 36in), lower table height, remove clutter from path, front-desk escort. Noted.
Nora K.: He asked for a private check-in at reception to avoid crowds and to have his chair stored in a secure area when not in use.
reception-bot: Front desk will pre-print a "Private Check-in" badge and hold wheelchair in Secure Storage Rack A. Reception will meet candidate at East Garage elevator and escort to lab.
Dev (Recruiter): Mateo also asked about lunch: he's halal + needs low-sodium option. Can we handle both?
Aisha (People Ops): Catering can do Halal + low-sodium box. We'll label it "Mateo V - Halal, Low Sodium" and confirm cross-contamination precautions.
Nora K.: He requested the coding test keyboard to be left-handed mechanical (ISO layout) and a vertical mouse. Are these available?
Facilities Bot: We have a left-handed Dactyl-like mechanical keyboard in Assets Locker 4 and a vertical ergonomic mouse. Reserving and labeling "Mateo V". We'll also leave a spare USB-C adapter and a disinfecting wipe.
Dev (Recruiter): One small policy ask: Mateo wants a brief 15-minute informal chat with the hiring manager after the loop (not evaluative) and asked if we can reimburse overnight pet boarding for his dog for the travel night. Any caps?
Aisha (People Ops): Informal 15-min chat OK (mark as non-evaluative). Pet boarding: we occasionally approve one-off pet boarding reimbursements up to $100 for candidates with extenuating travel constraints. Approving up to $100; ask for receipt.
Nora K.: He also asked whether we can provide printed materials in large font (14pt+) for the behavioral packet.
Aisha (People Ops): We'll print behavioral packet in 14pt Arial and include an electronic copy in high-contrast PDF. Attach to calendar note and hand a printed copy at check-in.
accessibility-bot: Reminder set: accessibility rep to meet Mateo 10 minutes before start to run through room setup and assistive hardware.
reception-bot: Badge printed with "Private Check-in" note; Secure Storage Rack A tag printed; parking voucher for van with ramp reserved at East Garage.
Dev (Recruiter): Great. I'll message Mateo with the elevator escort, keyboard/mouse confirmation, Windows machine info, lunch, pet-boarding reimbursement terms, and the private check-in details. Thanks all.
Aisha (People Ops): Closing loop  will follow up with vendor receipts if any and leave a contact number in the calendar note for day-of assistance. :white_check_mark:
